cohort: 210 low birth weight infants admitted to a neonatal intensive care unit
finding: The overall prevalence of intraventricular hemorrhage was 44.3%, with higher prevalence in very low birth weight infants, and risk factors included very low birth weight, extreme prematurity, HIV exposure, outborn delivery, and blood transfusion, while Cesarean delivery was protective.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was a protective factor against intraventricular hemorrhage.
